cases.scenario: Create a three-item bullet list with a link in the middle item. Indent a consecutive pair, add a third level, then outdent the innermost item using both keyboard and toolbar commands.
expected: The editor exposes the resulting hierarchy as nested lists, and each moved item keeps its text, link, order and selection offset.
An indent without an eligible predecessor leaves the document and history unchanged. Undo and redo retrace the admitted moves in order.

cases.scenario: Convert a selected run of bullet items to an ordered list between two unrelated blocks. Toggle the run back to paragraphs, then restore the list with undo and reopen the saved document.
expected: The selected items gain sequential markers in selection order. Each child list retains its type, nesting and content.
The adjacent blocks preserve their structure and identities, and the reopened document retains the restored list and its undo and redo history.

cases.scenario: Split a formatted list item with Enter, join the results with Backspace, then use Tab and Shift+Tab on an item at its first and last legal nesting levels. Repeat with an empty final item.
expected: The split and join preserve text, inline formatting and descendant order, and land the caret at the expected split or join boundary.
Keyboard actions honor level limits. Leaving a list through its empty final item places the caret in the resulting paragraph.

cases.scenario: Insert a task list containing a parent and a nested child. Toggle the parent by pointer and the child by keyboard. Read the document, copy it to another supported editor, then try toggling in read-only mode.
expected: Each checkbox has an accessible name and independent checked state. The copied list preserves both checked states and the parent-child relationship.
Each editable toggle is an undoable change. The read-only control conveys checked state and rejects attempts to change it.

cases.scenario: While one replica is offline, change the checked state of a task and move the same task beneath another item from the connected replica. Reconnect, undo the checked-state edit at its author, then reopen both peers.
expected: The replicas converge on one task at the new location with the admitted checked state. The task identity and its children remain stable.
Author-local undo restores the earlier checked state while retaining the other person's move, and both peers recover the same tree.

cases.scenario: Set an ordered list to start at 4. Split it with a paragraph, continue numbering in the tail, then explicitly restart the tail at 1. Export and reimport the result with a fresh editor.
expected: The first run starts at 4, the continued run starts at its computed next value, and the explicit restart overrides continuation.
The visible markers and exported numbering semantics agree. Invalid starts produce a reported refusal or documented loss, and preserve the prior native numbering.

cases.scenario: Create a three-item upper-Roman list with an explicit start of 8 and enable reverse counting. Insert an item in the middle, undo, and compare local, shared and static output.
expected: The original markers are VIII, VII and VI. The insertion extends the descending sequence without changing its start or style.
Local, shared and static output agree on markers, and undo restores the original sequence and numbering settings.

cases.scenario: Use different allowed bullet markers at two nesting levels, then switch the child marker style. Copy and paste the list into a fresh editor before saving and exporting.
expected: Changing the child style preserves the parent marker and item structure. The admitted markers survive copy, reopen and HTML export.
Values outside the documented marker set follow the same refusal or loss-reporting policy on toolbar, import and restore paths.

cases.scenario: Set an ordered list to a supported zero-padded counter style and assign a different explicit ordinal to its second item. Reorder the item and test marker output in the editor and interchange.
expected: The displayed sequence follows the documented style, override and reorder rules, and the override remains attached to its intended item.
The stored profile retains the values exactly. Export preserves supported semantics and identifies any target format that cannot represent them.

cases.scenario: Create a list item with a heading, paragraph, nested list and trailing paragraph. Join an empty neighboring item into the multi-block item, split a later empty paragraph back out, and repeat with an equivalent task item.
expected: The structural commands change only the intended item boundary and preserve all blocks in order, including the paragraph after the child list.
Undo restores the original item boundaries and checkbox state, and supported interchange preserves the list hierarchy and block order.

cases.scenario: Import a list with an item that skips an intermediate nesting level. Indent and outdent around the gap, save, reopen, and export to HTML and a target with limited nesting support.
expected: The model preserves the admitted depth gap and its descendant order. The UI, keyboard navigation and assistive technology expose only authored items.
Allowed export and import preserve the original depth gap. The limited target reports the specific approximation or unsupported structure.

cases.scenario: Create a legal numbered list with expected second-level markers 2.1 and 2.2 and a third-level marker 2.2.1. Move the 2.2 subtree beneath a different parent, reopen in another client, and export.
expected: The affected descendants' markers are recomputed from their new parent. Unaffected branches retain their legal numbering.
Clients recover the same numbering configuration and marker sequence, and supported portable export retains the configuration independently of local presentation options.

cases.scenario: Select two eligible blocks with different alignments. Apply center and then justify from the keyboard-accessible control, save, and inspect the restored editing view and static output.
expected: The control reports mixed state before the edit, then reports the value applied to both blocks. Adjacent ineligible content retains its layout.
The first Undo restores center alignment on both blocks. The second restores the distinct starting values. The resulting alignment is identical after restore and HTML interchange.

cases.scenario: Indent a left-to-right paragraph and a right-to-left paragraph containing mixed-script text. Change one direction, outdent it, and compare alignment, caret order and exported layout.
expected: Indent is applied to the paragraph's logical start edge, and changing direction updates that edge while preserving logical text order, selection and inline marks.
Indent controls stop at documented minimum and maximum levels. Round-trip retains the admitted direction and indentation.

cases.scenario: Apply two admitted line heights to otherwise identical multiline paragraphs in local and shared editors, then reset one paragraph to the inherited value and export.
expected: With font and viewport fixed, adjacent baselines measurably reflect each selected line height. Reset uses the documented inherited spacing.
Remote edits and reopen preserve the exact admitted value. Unsupported imported values receive a diagnostic and preserve valid text and layout fields.

cases.scenario: With the Markdown typing profile enabled, type approved heading, quote, code, list and inline-format markers one at a time. Include lookalike sequences in code and in the middle of a paragraph.
expected: Each eligible marker produces the documented native block or mark. Each excluded marker remains literal.
Undo first rolls back the conversion to the literal typed text. Undoing the preceding input follows the configured typing history.

cases.scenario: Type an eligible rule at a caret, then insert the same characters via composition, a literal-text paste and a remote edit already admitted by a replica using the disabled rules profile. Reopen each replica after synchronization.
expected: Only the eligible local typing path fires the rule. Composition and literal insertion retain the intended characters, and applying a remote edit does not run a local input rule on its contents.
Peers converge once per admitted operation. Reopening does not run the rules again, and replay preserves the source edit and conversion history.

cases.scenario: Type an approved marker after a matching list, type another after an unlike list, and enter a task marker inside an existing bullet item. Compare changes in local and shared editors.
expected: A matching continuation joins according to the active rule set, while the unlike list and its neighbors keep their identities and structure.
A permitted task conversion retains the existing item text and descendants. Undo restores the literal marker and prior structure in the same edit path.

cases.scenario: In English and French profiles, type quoted text, contractions, an ellipsis, spaced dashes, fractions and arrows. Repeat with one rule disabled and with mixed-direction text around the caret.
expected: The profile emits the specified Unicode code points for each admitted replacement, including required nonbreaking spaces. Disabled rules and out-of-context tokens remain literal.
Formatting and selection offsets map correctly around each replacement. One undo restores the original typed characters and redo restores the replacement.

cases.scenario: Set a host-configured replacement for an approved trigger, disable a built-in rule, and type both sequences with and without the configured boundary. Try to enable a conflicting rule and open the confirmed profile on a second replica.
expected: Eligible input uses the configured output. Disabled or boundary-excluded sequences remain literal and conflicting configurations have a documented deterministic outcome.
Undo restores the exact input, and the peer presents the admitted change without recomputing it from its own rule options.

cases.scenario: Use the keyboard to open the picker, locate a character by name and by Unicode code point, then insert it into selected formatted text. Repeat using a host-provided character group.
expected: The picker identifies and inserts the actual Unicode character, including on narrow screens and with keyboard-only navigation. Insertion respects the current formatting and selection.
Undo restores the previous text and marks. Closing without a selection leaves document history unchanged and returns focus to the editor.

cases.scenario: Apply upper, lower and title case to a selection with German sharp S, Greek sigma and Turkish dotted and dotless I, surrounded by independently marked text. Repeat with and without the explicit Turkish locale in a shared session.
expected: The output follows the chosen locale and case mode, and remaps the selection and format boundaries when the Unicode length changes.
Peers converge on the same text and untouched neighboring marks. A single undo restores the original characters and exact format boundaries.

cases.scenario: Capture admitted inline formatting from a source selection and paint a destination once. Enable continuous painting for two additional selections, then cancel and change the selection again.
expected: Each destination gains the admitted source formats while retaining its own text, structure and unrelated semantics. Single-use painting disarms after one application.
Continuous mode applies until cancellation, and each completed application is independently undoable.

cases.scenario: Configure a named formatting preset for two admitted styles and an ineligible selection. Apply it from the named picker, inspect its active state and export and reopen the result.
expected: Applying the named preset gives the selected eligible content the configured appearance and preserves the text. Ineligible content has a documented scoped refusal or remains unchanged.
Undo reverses the preset application as one edit, and the selected representation restores consistently under the documented host preset and interchange contract.
